title: Yesterday I…
goal: Talk about past events with the passé composé, using the helper verb avoir.
bekal: forming the past participle of the three verb groups
putting negatives and adverbs in the right place
wave: Review **Unit 17** first: give directions from your home to three different places, all in the *vous* imperative.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ?
dialogs.intro: Monday morning. Thomas asks Budi about his weekend.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Alors, qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ?
lines.id: So, what did you do yesterday?
lines.literal: so, what is-it-that you have done yesterday?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: J'ai visité le musée des Beaux-Arts.
lines.id: I visited the Museum of Fine Arts.
lines.literal: I-have visited the museum of-the beautiful-arts.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.id: Oh yeah? Did you like it?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Beaucoup. J'ai passé trois heures là-bas.
lines.id: A lot. I spent three hours there.
lines.literal: much. I-have spent three hours there.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Tu as vu l'exposition sur Monet ?
lines.id: Did you see the Monet exhibition?
lines.literal: you have seen the exhibition on Monet?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Oui ! J'ai pris beaucoup de photos.
lines.id: Yes! I took lots of photos.
lines.literal: yes! I-have taken many of photos.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Et après, tu as mangé quelque part ?
lines.id: And afterwards, did you eat somewhere?
lines.literal: and after, you have eaten something part?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: J'ai dîné avec Camille. On a essayé un vietnamien.
lines.id: I had dinner with Camille. We tried a Vietnamese place.
lines.literal: I-have dined with Camille. one has tried a Vietnamese.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Excellent. Mais je n'ai pas fini mon plat.
lines.id: Delicious. But I didn't finish my plate.
lines.literal: excellent. but I not-have not finished my dish.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Tu n'as jamais assez faim, toi !
lines.literal: you not-have never enough hunger, you!

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Et toi ? Tu as travaillé tout le week-end ?
lines.id: What about you? Did you work all weekend?
lines.literal: and you? you have worked all the weekend?

notes: **The passé composé is built from two pieces:** the present of *avoir* + the past participle. *J'**ai** mang**é***, *tu **as** fin**i***, *il **a** attend**u***. Only *avoir* changes with the subject; the participle stays put — much like English "I have eaten", "she has eaten".
**Regular past participles follow their group:** -er → **-é**, -ir → **-i**, -re → **-u**. Those three endings cover most verbs.
**With avoir, the past participle doesn't change.** *Elle a mangé*, *ils ont mangé*, *elles ont mangé* — all *mangé*. This will be different in Unit 20, when the helper verb is *être*.
**The negative wraps around the helper verb only.** *Je **n'**ai **pas** fini*, not *je n'ai fini pas*. The second part of the negative sits between *avoir* and the participle.
**Short adverbs slip into the same gap.** *J'ai **déjà** mangé*, *il a **bien** dormi*, *tu as **trop** bu*. Long ones stay at the end: *j'ai mangé **rapidement***.

**C'était** is a past form of *être* from the *imparfait* family, which is A2 material. But it's so common (*c'était bien*, *c'était bon*, *c'était super*) that you should learn it now as one fixed chunk.

grammars.title: Forming the past participle
body: Three regular endings, then a list of irregulars to memorize. Luckily the list is short and full of verbs you've already used many times.
after: ⚠️ Every -er verb sounds the same in the infinitive and the past participle: *parler* and *parlé* are both pahr-LAY. Only the helper verb tells them apart. This is the spelling trap that shows up most in exams.
The past of reflexive verbs uses *être* and is covered in Unit 20.

grammars.title: Irregular past participles to memorize
body: Eighteen verbs that cover most everyday talk about the past.
after: A rough but helpful pattern: many end in **-u** (*vu, bu, pu, lu, su, reçu, connu, voulu*), a group ends in **-is** (*pris, mis, compris, appris*), and a small group ends in **-ert** (*ouvert, offert*).
*Eu* is pronounced just **ü** — the e is completely silent. One of the most deceptive spellings in French.

grammars.title: Where negatives and adverbs go
body: They all slip into the gap between the helper verb and the past participle.
after: ⚠️ *Ne… personne* is the exception: *personne* goes **after** the participle. *Je n'ai vu **personne***, not *je n'ai personne vu*.
Time words (*hier, la semaine dernière, il y a deux jours*) can go at the start or the end of the sentence, but never in the gap.

blocks.text: ⚠️ *Il y a* has two completely different jobs: "there is" (Unit 10) and "ago" (here). *Il y a une pharmacie* = there's a pharmacy; *il y a deux jours* = two days ago. The only difference is what follows — a place noun or a length of time.

blocks.title: Asking about the past
items: *Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ?* — What did you do yesterday?
*Tu as bien dormi ?* — Did you sleep well?
*Tu es déjà allé en France ?* — Have you ever been to France?
*Ça s'est bien passé ?* — Did it go well?

exercises.prompt: Put into the past with avoir.
Write the past participle of these verbs.

answers: J'ai mangé au restaurant. — Tu as fini ton travail. — Il a attendu le bus. — Nous avons visité le musée. — Vous avez choisi un dessert. — Elles ont répondu à la question.
fait — vu — pris — bu — écrit — eu
Je n'ai pas fini mon plat. — Il n'a pas vu l'exposition. — Nous n'avons pas mangé. — Tu n'as pas compris la question. — Elle n'a pas pris de photos.
Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ? — J'ai visité le musée. — J'ai pris beaucoup de photos. — J'ai dîné avec Camille. — Je n'ai pas fini mon plat.
